brief: Wolfe Research addresses the NVDA CEO situation after NY Times reporting that CEO Jensen Huang also had an affair with a subordinate executive, which Wolfe says makes it more challenging, though not impossible, for NVDA's board to keep him. The board met the evening before this November 12, 2026 note, and Wolfe thinks an announcement is possible as early as the day of publication. Media reports say the board is already working with an outside firm on replacement candidates. If Huang steps down, Wolfe sees zero impact on fundamentals, earnings or orders through at least CY28, since NVDA is sold out and its roadmap already runs that far. Huang is key person risk because he identified AI's direction early, as he did in graphics, but NVDA's IP, software and engineering talent would remain, limiting the damage to a multiple discount that is hard to size, and much of it may already be priced in given the stock trades under 8x Wolfe's FY29 earnings view. Separately, Wolfe dismisses export-control worries: NVDA's China AI shipments are de minimis, and China already restricts use of the US-permitted H200, so further controls would change little. Rating: Outperform, $275 target, 58.3% upside.
